FROM (

    JOIN drug d2 ON pat1.drug_id = d2.id
    WHERE LOWER(d2.generic_name) LIKE '%statin%'
       OR LOWER(d2.brand_name) LIKE '%statin%'
       OR LOWER(d2.drug_class) LIKE '%statin%'
       OR d2.ndc IN (SELECT drug FROM statin_drugs)  -- would need lookup
    
) pat3

    SELECT concept_id FROM omop.concept 
    WHERE LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%simvastatin%' 
       OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%atorvastatin%' 
       OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%rosuvastatin%' 
       OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%pravastatin%' 
       OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%lovastatin%'
)

content.text: The previous query returned ~26K statin-related concept ancestors (all levels of the statin hierarchy). Now I'll use this to count patients. Given the massive result, I'll query directly against `drug_exposure` using a subquery pattern that SQL Server can handle efficiently.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT person_id) AS statin_patients_past_year
FROM omop.drug_exposure
WHERE drug_concept_id IN (
    SELECT ancestor_concept_id 
    FROM omop.concept_ancestor 
    WHERE descendant_concept_id IN (
        SELECT concept_id FROM omop.concept 
        WHERE LOWER(CONCEPT_NAME) LIKE '%simvastatin%' 
           OR LOWER(CONCEPT_NAME) LIKE '%atorvastatin%' 
           OR LOWER(CONCEPT_NAME) LIKE '%rosuvastatin%' 
           OR LOWER(CONCEPT_NAME) LIKE '%pravastatin%' 
           OR LOWER(CONCEPT_NAME) LIKE '%lovastatin%'
    )
)
AND date_of_exposure >= DATEADD(year, -1, GETDATE())
